title: Serving runtime: architecture, kernel scheduling, profiling & benchmarks, runbooks
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Serving Runtime architecture, kernel scheduling policy, profiling playbooks, benchmarking suite guidance, recent release notes, known issues, and day-to-day runbooks. It is the canonical reference for engineers operating or extending Redwood's inference runtime.

Sections
1) Runtime architecture overview
2) Kernel scheduling: policies and heuristics
3) Profiling playbook (how-to)
4) Benchmarking suite: workloads, metrics, and expected targets
5) Release notes (v2028.07.01)
6) Known issues & mitigations
7) Runbooks and operational procedures
8) Team wiki & ownership

1) Runtime architecture overview

Short summary
- Service name: rw-inferd (primary inference daemon).
- Core responsibilities: request ingress, dynamic batching, KV cache management, kernel dispatch, model variant routing, telemetry emission.
- Deployment topologies: Hosted API pool, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC on-prem images).

Components
- Frontend router (rw-router): HTTP/gRPC ingress, auth, tenant routing, and quick-path for cached prefixes.
- Orchestration (rw-orch): selects model variant, placement, and batch formation policy.
- Worker runtime (rw-worker): process per-GPU for A100/H100/RTX series, handles CUDA context, kernel scheduling, and quantized execution paths.
- KV cache service (rw-kvcache): persistent Redis-backed LRU cache for prefix KV shards; local in-memory adapters on rw-worker for hot prefixes.
- Telemetry emitter (rw-metrics): emits per-request traces, token-level cost breakdown, GPU utilization, kernel queue lengths.

Design decisions & rationale
- Continuous batching: we use a latency-aware batching loop (max_batch_size & max_queue_delay) to balance throughput and tail latency. Default: max_batch_size=64, max_queue_delay=6ms.
- Kernel specialization: separate execution paths for fp16, int8/4 quantized kernels. Kernel selection is decided by rw-worker at model load-time using a small benchmark suite (see benchmarking section).
- Cold start handling: model weights use segmented loading and a small warmup micro-batch to populate KV cache before accepting production traffic.

SLOs and targets (example)
- 95th percentile generation latency for 512-token requests: <= 120ms (hosted, A100); Dedicated SLOs negotiated in contracts.
- Median token generation throughput per GPU (A100-80GB, int8): >= 250 tokens/sec under steady-state workloads.
- Availability (rw-inferd pool): 99.95% monthly.

2) Kernel scheduling: policies and heuristics

Goal
- Maximize GPU utilization while respecting latency SLOs, tenant isolation, and fairness.

Key concepts
- Kernel queue: per-GPU prioritized queue of kernel launches (attention, FFN, softmax, GEMM).
- Preemption points: inter-batch boundaries only. We do not preempt mid-kernel.
- Co-location policy: small low-latency workloads (<= 64 tokens) are colocated; long-running high-memory workloads are isolated to dedicated GPUs.

Scheduling heuristics (rw-sched):
- Priority classes: realtime (prod low-latency paths), burst (short job bursts), background (batch evals and offline workloads).
- Admission controls: if queue_length > QH(90)=120 kernels or estimated_queue_delay > 60ms for realtime class, reject or fall back to a cheaper model variant.
- Kernel fusion ordering: schedule attention->ffn fusion candidates first to reduce kernel launch overhead for medium sequence lengths (>=256).

Placement & co-location rules
- Prefer colocating compatible memory profiles: colocate int8/4 quantized workloads together.
- Avoid colocating large model shards with high-IO prefetch tasks.
- Soft isolation: use cgroups + CUDA MPS in combination with rw-sched fairness tokens.

Eviction and throttling
- Evict policy for idle prefixes: retain hot prefixes for 5 minutes; cold eviction after 30 minutes during memory pressure.
- Throttling: when GPU mem_util > 88% and swap risk detected, throttle background class to 10% of capacity.

Metrics emitted for scheduling decisions
- per_gpu_kernel_queue_length, per_gpu_estimated_queue_delay_ms, per_tenant_avg_latency_ms, per_tenant_tokens_per_second, gpu_memory_reserved_bytes.

3) Profiling playbook (how-to)

Purpose
- Reproduce performance regressions and identify kernel-level bottlenecks.

Prerequisites
- Access to staging GPU pool (tag: staging-infer), perf role.
- Tools: nvprof/nsight systems, CUPTI-based tracer, Triton-style micro-bench harness, rw-benchmark CLI.

Step-by-step profiling
1. Reproduce baseline: run rw-benchmark --model <model> --batch 1 --tokens 512 --warmup 50 --iters 200 and capture latency and tok/s.
2. Capture GPU traces: nsys profile -o trace -t cuda,osrt --trace-fork-before-exec --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --rw-inferd -- rw-benchmark ...
3. Capture kernel-level timings: use CUDA CUPTI to record kernel durations and occupancy. Example (simplified): nvprof --print-gpu-trace --csv --log-file nvprof.csv rw-benchmark ...
4. Identify hotspots: correlate long kernels with ops (GEMM attention, layernorm). Use symbol mapping produced by rw-worker (artifact: /var/log/rw-worker/kernel-symbols-<model>.map).
5. Test mitigations: increase batch size to amortize kernel launch, try kernel fusion flags (env RW_KERNEL_FUSE=1), test quantized path (rw-worker --enable-quant int8).
6. Validate: re-run baseline and ensure 95p latency regression is resolved or documented.

Quick checklist
- Collect: nsys trace, nvprof csv, rw-metrics exporter dump, rw-worker logs, model-config (yaml).
- Always attach trace id to issue and link traces in internal ticket.

4) Benchmarking suite: workloads, metrics, and expected targets

Workloads included in repo: infra/benchmarks/serving-suite
- Small chat: 1-4 prompt turns, median length 64 tokens.
- Standard generation: 512-token generation with 0.7 temperature.
- Embeddings: batch_embedding size 32, embedding dim 2048.
- Reranking: 32 candidates, pairwise scoring.

Metrics collected
- throughput_tokens_per_second (tokens/s), p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, gpu_util_pct, avg_gpu_memory_bytes, kernel_launchs_per_request.

How to run (example)
- rw-benchmark run --suite standard-generation --model <model> --gpu-type a100 --quant int8 --out results.json
- CI nightly: bench-runner.sh --ci --models "all-curated" --workloads "small-chat,standard-generation" --retain 30d

Acceptance targets (guidance)
- A100 int8 standard-generation (512 tokens): p95 <= 120ms, throughput >= 250 tok/s.
- H100 fp16 small-chat (64 tokens): p95 <= 35ms.
- Embeddings batch 32: tokens/s equivalent throughput >= 3000 vectors/sec for 1536-dim embeddings.

Benchmarking notes
- Always set --warmup 100 to stabilize kernel caches.
- Compare against last release baseline stored in benchmarking dashboard (Grafana board: infra.bench.serving).

5) Release notes (v2028.07.01)

Highlights
- Kernel scheduler (rw-sched) v1.4: improved fusion ordering heuristics and new admission control for realtime class to reduce p95 latency under bursty traffic.
- New quantized int4 kernels: experimental path enabled behind feature flag RW_ENABLE_INT4=true (opt-in).
- Profiling tooling: updated nsys trace wrapper and automatic symbolizer for rw-worker (fixes mis-mapped kernel names).
- Telemetry: added per-kernel latency histograms and per-request kernel_count metric.

Upgrade notes
- Rolling upgrade supported. Steps: 1) Deploy rw-sched v1.4 to orchestration control plane, 2) Gradually roll rw-worker v2.8 to worker pools (canaries 5%), 3) Monitor grafana infra.bench.serving p95 and per_gpu_queue_length for 30m, 4) If regressions > 10% roll back rw-worker.

Known compatibility changes
- Default max_queue_delay reduced from 8ms to 6ms; workloads tuned for previous default may see slightly lower throughput but improved tail latency.

6) Known issues & mitigations

Issue: Occasional p95 spikes during multi-tenant bursts
- Symptom: p95 latency jumps ~2x for 5-15 minutes after large model loads.
- Root cause (typical): simultaneous model shard prefetch and KV cache population causing GPU memory pressure and elevated kernel queue.
- Workaround: enable proactive shard prefetch in off-peak with rw-orch flag --prefetch-window=300s or evict low-use prefixes earlier (set KVCACHE_HOT_TTL=120s).

Issue: Mis-leading kernel names in nsys traces (older workers)
- Symptom: traces show generic kernel symbols (e.g., unnamed_kernel).
- Mitigation: upgrade rw-worker >= v2.7 or run symbolizer post-processing: rw-symbolize --input trace.qdrep --symbols /var/log/rw-worker/kernel-symbols-<model>.map

Issue: Int4 path causes occasional coherence faults on H100 driver older than 535.x
- Mitigation: pin driver to >= 535.14 for H100; feature gate RW_ENABLE_INT4=false until driver upgraded.

7) Runbooks and operational procedures

Common oncall playbook (short)
1. Alert: p95_latency_inferd_prod > 2x baseline for > 5m.
2. Triage: identify impacted model(s) and tenant(s) using rw-query-metrics --window 10m --filter p95>baseline*2.
3. Check scheduler queue: rw-admin inspect-queue --gpu <id>. If per_gpu_estimated_queue_delay_ms > 150ms, consider throttling background class: rw-admin set-class-quota background 0.1
4. If memory pressure: run rw-admin evict-prefixes --age-gt 1800 --dry-run and then without --dry-run if safe.
5. Rollback path: for regressions after worker upgrade, set canary to 0% via rw-orch rollback --component rw-worker --version <previous>.

Post-incident checklist
- Collect traces (nsys, nvprof), metrics dumps, worker logs, and open postmortem if impact > 1 customer-hour.
- Add reproduction steps to infra/benchmarks/serving-suite and schedule a regression test.

8) Team wiki & ownership

Primary owners
- Serving runtime (rw-team): engineering (owner: Asha Patel).
- Observability & metrics: eng-platform (owner: Daniel Kim).
- Oncall rotation: eng-sre (contact: slo-oncall@redwood.ai).

Where to find artifacts
- Benchmarks repo: git@repo:redwood/infra/benchmarks/serving-suite (branch: main).
- Worker logs: s3://redwood-logs/serving-workers/<cluster>/<date>/
- Kernel symbol maps: /var/log/rw-worker/kernel-symbols-<model>.map on worker nodes and archived to s3.

Contributing guidelines
- Changes to kernel scheduling heuristics require: ADR, microbench results, and a canary rollout plan. See infra/adr/kernel-scheduling-2027.md.
- Profiling additions: include a repro dataset, nsys trace, and a before/after benchmark in the PR.

Appendix: useful CLI commands and snippets
- Run a quick benchmark:
  rw-benchmark --model redwood/llama-4x --batch 8 --tokens 512 --quant int8 --warmup 100 --iters 500 --output /tmp/bench.json

- Inspect queues on GPU 3:
  rw-admin inspect-queue --gpu 3 --json | jq .

- Evict cold prefixes (example):
  rw-admin evict-prefixes --age-gt 1800 --force --prefix-summary > /tmp/evict.log

- Example model config excerpt (YAML):
  model: redwood/llama-4x
  max_batch_size: 64
  max_queue_delay_ms: 6
  preferred_quant: int8
  warmup_microbatch: 2

Contact and escalation
- Oncall (primary): eng-sre team (pager: see oncall rota).
- Escalation for infra incidents: Eng Platform -> Head of SRE -> CTO.
